architecture_decisions: Keep safe proposal validation and all mutation authority unchanged; expose only bounded router failure classification and feed static validator-specific repair guidance to the next already-admitted candidate after VALIDATION_EXHAUSTED.
work_items: Project bounded routing failure diagnostics across the implementation-generation boundary.
Add validator-guided alternate-candidate repair constraints without increasing retry bounds.
Add focused regression tests for classification, guidance, provider separation, finite recovery, and bounded evidence.
validations: AC-01: ImplementationGenerationFailure exposes bounded router failure classification without raw provider/model output.
AC-02: A proposal-validator rejection supplies static safe-patch repair guidance to the next admitted candidate for the same work unit.
AC-03: Provider/rate-limit failures do not receive validator-specific guidance.
AC-04: Repair guidance reinforces exact path/digest binding and strict single-file unified-diff requirements.
AC-05: Existing max_reassignments_per_work_unit and eligible-agent bounds remain unchanged.
AC-06: Repair guidance grants no canonical source, lineage, Git, deployment, REVIEW, run-transition, credential, or network authority.
AC-07: Exhaustion evidence remains bounded and records only server-owned rejection kind values.
AC-08: First-candidate success path is unchanged.
AC-09: Focused regression tests prove the new classification and recovery behavior.
AC-10: Protected spec/plan validation and all release gates are green before merge.
risks: Static guidance may not repair every malformed candidate; the run must still fail closed after the existing finite candidate budget rather than weakening validation.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Failure classification survives generation boundary
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: ImplementationGenerationFailure exposes bounded router failure classification without raw provider/model output.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Validation-only repair guidance
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: A parsed proposal rejected by the protected proposal validator causes the next admitted candidate for the same work unit to receive static server-owned safe-patch repair guidance.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Provider-failure separation
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: Provider/rate-limit failures do not receive validator-specific repair guidance and remain governed by existing recovery semantics.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Strict contract reinforcement
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: Repair guidance states the exact safe-patch requirements needed by the unchanged server validator.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Finite recovery preserved
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: The existing max_reassignments_per_work_unit bound and eligible-agent set remain authoritative.

protected_acceptance_map.title: No authority expansion
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: Repair guidance grants no canonical source, lineage, Git, deployment, REVIEW, Engineering Run transition, credential, or network authority.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Bounded exhaustion evidence
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: Exhaustion evidence records only bounded server-owned rejection kind values and preserves worker_process_loss=false with all mutation claims false.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Success-path parity
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: A first candidate that passes the protected proposal validator follows the existing path with no repair guidance or semantic change.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Regression proof
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: Tests prove validation classification, validation-guided next-candidate repair, provider-failure separation, finite recovery, and bounded diagnostics.

protected_acceptance_map.title: Release gates
protected_acceptance_map.protected_requirement: Protected spec/plan validation, focused tests, full API regression, Bounded Autonomy, client/browser, protected promotion, and DSPy release gates are green before merge.

critique: The design intentionally does not weaken the validator or add extra retries; if static guidance is insufficient, production evidence should drive a separately governed deterministic proposal-construction improvement.
